findings.title: A statement that prints a page subtotal labelled "Total" is refused outright, with a message blaming the column mapping
findings.evidence: domain/banking/tie_out.py:190-206 — printed_totals iterates rows and RETURNS THE FIRST row whose cell[0] matches _TOTAL_LABEL (`^\s*(grand\s+)?totals?\s*:?\s*$`, normalizer.py:75) and carries exactly two numeric cells. A per-page or per-month subtotal labelled "Total" satisfies both. statement_check (tie_out.py:302-319) then treats the mismatch as `tot_bad` and routers/banking.py:851-853 raises HTTPException(422) BEFORE anything is written. I reproduced it end to end in this session: a 6-column cheque-layout CSV with a page "Total" row before the real "Grand Total" parsed all 3 rows correctly and came back `verified: False`, refusal = 'This statement does not match its own "Total" row: deposits came to ₹500.00 against the statement's ₹0.00. Either some lines were not read, or a column is mapped to the wrong thing. Nothing has been imported.' There is no server-side override: `overrideBalance` in apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:583,992 gates only the client-side balance_check, and no form field skips the totals check.
findings.ca_experience: The CA uploads a perfectly good statement and cannot import it at all. The refusal tells them to check the debit/credit column mapping — when no mapping was involved and nothing was misread. The only way past it is to edit the bank's file by hand. Per-page and per-month subtotals labelled "Total" are common in Indian bank PDF and Excel exports, so this can block a client's whole month.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime cannot import a PDF statement at all and its Excel import simply skips rows it cannot parse. Zoho Books and QuickBooks skip non-transaction rows silently and never block an import on a totals row. No competitor refuses an import because it read a subtotal.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the LAST matching totals row rather than the first, and prefer a row whose label literally contains "grand". Better: collect every candidate totals row and only use one if exactly one of them equals the parsed sums, or if it is the last row of the file. Also add a `skip_totals_check` acknowledgement path so a CA who has compared the figures by eye is never stuck — the refusal should be a stop, not a wall.

findings.title: Overdraft and Cash Credit bank accounts are given an Asset ledger, and the ledger picker will not offer a Liability one
findings.evidence: migrations/054_v13_payroll_assets_banking.sql:100-101 — bank_accounts.account_type CHECK allows 'Current','Savings','Cash Credit','Overdraft'. apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:415-417 offers all four in the form. But routers/banking.py:222-253 `_ensure_bank_ledger` hardcodes `"account_type": "Asset", "account_subtype": "Bank"` for the auto-created ledger, and AccountsPanel.tsx:339-342 filters the manual ledger picker with `.eq("account_type", "Asset")`. I grepped the whole banking backend for `account_type` (services/bank_*.py, services/banking_service.py, routers/banking.py, domain/banking/*.py): the bank account's own account_type is read NOWHERE — only the chart account's is.
findings.ca_experience: Almost every Indian SME runs a Cash Credit or Overdraft limit. Its statement imports and posts fine, but the utilised limit sits as a NEGATIVE ASSET on the balance sheet instead of under Schedule III "Short-term borrowings". Current assets are overstated (understated by a negative), current liabilities are understated, and the current ratio in the ratio report is wrong. The CA cannot fix it from the UI: the ledger picker refuses to show a Liability account.
findings.market_standard: Tally requires a Bank OD/CC account to be created under the "Bank OD A/c" group, which is a Loans (Liability) group, and reports it under short-term borrowings. Zoho Books and Busy both classify an OD/CC ledger as a liability.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `_ensure_bank_ledger` read the account_type: create a Liability / 'Bank OD' subtype ledger for 'Cash Credit' and 'Overdraft', an Asset / 'Bank' one otherwise. Widen the ledger picker's filter to Asset OR Liability-with-a-bank-subtype. Add a Schedule III mapping so the balance lands under short-term borrowings, and a migration to re-classify existing OD/CC ledgers with a report of what moved.

findings.title: A foreign-currency bank account can be created, and its statement imports and posts to the ledger at 1:1 as if the amounts were rupees
findings.evidence: routers/banking.py:166-180 `_guard_foreign_bank_currency` explicitly PERMITS a non-INR bank account when multi-currency is active for the client, and routers/banking.py:441-447 stores it. routers/banking.py:615-646 `bank_account_balance` even reports a `foreign_balance_minor`. But the import path never reads the currency: services/banking_service.py:126-138 `import_normalized` stores `debit_paise`/`credit_paise`/`balance_paise` verbatim from the parser, and services/bank_posting_service.py:287-420 `_plan` builds lines with no currency or rate and calls `phase2_journal_service._create_journal` (bank_posting_service.py:558-565) without `txn_currency` — while that kernel does accept `txn_currency`/`exchange_rate` (phase2_journal_service.py:1523, 1589, 1688). I grepped services/bank_posting_service.py, services/banking_service.py and domain/banking/*.py for currency/fx/exchange handling in the import-and-post path: there is none.
findings.ca_experience: A client with a USD EEFC account: a $10,000 receipt imports as `credit_paise = 1000000` and posts as ₹10,000 instead of roughly ₹8.5 lakh. The bank ledger, the trial balance, the P&L and the cash-flow statement are all wrong by the exchange rate, and nothing on any screen says so. There is no FX revaluation of the bank balance at year end either.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books holds a base and a foreign amount per bank line and revalues foreign bank accounts at period close. Tally Prime records a forex bank ledger with rate-wise entries and produces a Forex Gain/Loss adjustment at year end.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) refuse a statement import for a non-INR bank account until the FX path exists — one line in `upload_statement`, and honest; or (b) carry the account's currency onto the parsed rows, ask for the rate per statement or per line, and pass `txn_currency`/`exchange_rate` into `_create_journal` the way the sales/purchase FX paths already do. (a) today, (b) when a client needs it.

findings.title: The "Bank Reconciliation Statement" is a statement-line tick-off; it has no unpresented cheques and no deposits in transit, which is what a BRS is
findings.evidence: domain/banking/reconciliation.py:19-50 — the whole tie-out is `opening + reconciled credits − reconciled debits ± adjustments == statement closing`. Every row in the report comes from services/bank_reconciliation_service.py:60-72 `_posted_account_txns`, which reads bank_transactions for the account's statements and keeps only those with a `posted_journal_id`. `_classify` (:84-100) buckets them as reconciled / unreconciled / exceptions — all three are STATEMENT lines. Nothing in the module reads journal_entries or journal_lines, so a cheque issued and entered in the books but not yet presented at the bank has no row anywhere in it, and neither does a deposit banked but not yet credited. services/bank_reconciliation_pdf_service.py:83-90 prints exactly those five tie-out rows under the title "Bank Reconciliation Statement".
findings.ca_experience: The CA opens Reconcile expecting the document they have prepared every month of their career — "Balance as per Cash Book … add cheques issued not presented … less cheques deposited not credited … Balance as per Pass Book" — and gets a tick-list plus a difference. At year end, the auditor's BRS working paper cannot be produced from this product at all, and the PDF it does produce is titled as if it were one. This is the single most recognisable accountant-facing artefact in the module and it is the wrong document.
findings.market_standard: Tally Prime's BRS is the reference implementation: it lists "Amounts not reflected in Bank" from the COMPANY BOOKS with instrument number and date, plus "Amounts not reflected in Company Books", and reconciles Balance as per Company Books to Balance as per Bank. Zoho Books, Busy and Marg all produce the two-sided statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the book side. Read the bank ledger's journal_lines for the period, subtract the lines that came from a posted bank_transaction, and what remains is the reconciling set: cheques issued not presented (credits to bank with no statement line) and deposits in transit (debits to bank with no statement line). Render the classic two-sided statement in the PDF, with the instrument number from `reference_no`. The existing tie-out stays as the internal check.

findings.title: "Adjustments" is an unexplained plug number that can force a reconciliation to tie out and produce a signed BRS PDF
findings.evidence: migrations/102_bank_reconciliation_b4.sql:20 adds `adjustments_paise bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` with no companion reason, narration or itemisation column. models/banking.py:353-358 `ReconciliationUpdateIn` accepts it as a bare Optional[int]. services/bank_reconciliation_service.py:294-304 `update_session` writes it with no validation and no audit call. domain/banking/reconciliation.py:39 folds it straight into `book_balance`, so `complete()` (bank_reconciliation_service.py:401-405) passes its `summary["reconciles"]` gate. The UI exposes it as a free text box: apps/web/components/banking/ReconcileTab.tsx:422-428 renders "Adjustment (₹)" and PATCHes `adjustments_paise`. The completion is then frozen into a snapshot and rendered by services/bank_reconciliation_pdf_service.py as a certified "Bank Reconciliation Statement". Contrast the reopen path, which DOES demand a ≥10-character reason enforced by a DB CHECK (models/banking.py:312-329).
findings.ca_experience: An Executive with `banking.write` who cannot find a ₹47,300 difference types 47300 into Adjustment, the tie-out goes green, Complete is enabled, and the firm now holds a certified reconciliation PDF whose "Adjustments" line means nothing. Nobody — including the partner reviewing it — can tell from the document what the ₹47,300 was.
findings.market_standard: Tally's BRS has no plug field at all; every difference must be an actual voucher or a bank date. Zoho Books requires you to either match a transaction or create one for the difference, and QuickBooks forces an explicit "reconciliation discrepancy" journal that posts to the ledger. None of them lets a number reconcile by assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a substantive reason for any non-zero adjustment (mirror `ReconciliationReopenIn.substantive` and back it with a DB CHECK), write an audit_log row when it changes, print the reason on the PDF beside the figure, and gate a non-zero adjustment on `banking.approve` (Manager+). Better still, make an adjustment an actual posted journal so the books and the reconciliation agree.

findings.title: There is no way to delete or undo a mis-imported statement — nothing in the backend or the UI
findings.evidence: routers/banking.py registers GET /statements (:1097) and POST /statements/import and /upload, but no DELETE. I grepped apps/api/routers/*.py for a bank_statements delete and apps/web for any `from("bank_statements")` write: there are none — the only DELETE in the module's api client is `deleteColumnMapping` (apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:954). The statements table in apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:235-252 offers exactly one action per row: "View". The import modal defaults the account to `accounts[0]?.id` (AccountsPanel.tsx:565), so picking the wrong bank is one careless click. The dedup hash includes bank_account_id (domain/banking/dedup.py:30-40), so re-importing to the CORRECT account works — and the wrong-account copy stays forever.
findings.ca_experience: A CA imports April's HDFC statement against the Cosmos account. 312 lines are now on the wrong bank, appear in the wrong Bank Book, will be offered to the wrong reconciliation, and permanently block that account's deletion (routers/banking.py:_DELETE_BLOCKERS). The only remedy in the product is to open each of the 312 lines and Set aside, and even then the statement row and its totals remain. Same problem for a statement imported under a wrong column mapping that passed the checks.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books lets you delete an uploaded statement and all its unreconciled transactions in one action. QuickBooks has "Undo" on a bank import batch. Tally's bank statement import can be reverted by deleting the imported vouchers as a set.
findings.suggested_fix: Add DELETE /statements/{id}, permitted only while every line on it is unposted and unreconciled, cascading to bank_transactions (the FK is already ON DELETE CASCADE), writing the whole statement header to audit_log first, and refusing with a named reason otherwise. Surface it as a Delete action on the statements table beside View.

findings.title: The Bank Book fetches every transaction on the account and computes the running balance in Python — the exact pattern CLAUDE.md forbids
findings.evidence: services/bank_register_service.py:60-84 `_txns` uses `fetch_all` to page EVERY bank_transaction for the account ('ALL of them — not just posted ones'), then :86-98 reads the reconciliation statuses, then domain/banking/register.py:146-205 `build_register` sorts the whole set and accumulates the balance row by row in Python, and only THEN does `_matches` filter and the service page. CLAUDE.md, "Reporting performance — the rule, not a preference": "No report may fetch rows proportional to transaction volume… Fetching raw rows and computing in Python is the third option and it is not available." The Bank Book is listed as a report (apps/web/app/clients/[id]/reports/page.tsx:119-121, under Operational). The same shape is in services/bank_reconciliation_service.py:60-72, which is called again by `opening_suggestion` (:164) on every session create.
findings.ca_experience: On the client CLAUDE.md already measured (12,836 entries), opening the Bank Book is thirteen Singapore→Mumbai round trips of 1,000 rows each before the first row renders. That is the same shape as the cash-flow report that measured 54.34s and could not finish inside lib/api's 45-second abort. A CA who opens Bank Book to look up one balance waits, or sees the generic error card.
findings.market_standard: Tally computes a bank ledger's running balance in its own engine over a memory-mapped company file — instant. Zoho Books pages the register server-side with the balance carried in the query.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the running balance into SQL, the way public.cash_flow_report (migration 277) and public.schedule_iii_ageing (migration 303) were moved: a SQL function returning finished register rows with a window-function running balance, plus the first-divergence probe. Keep domain/banking/register.py as the mock-mode twin and pin the two with a parity test, exactly as tests/test_cash_flow_sql_parity_pg.py does.

findings.title: The statement upload endpoint is `async def` but does blocking PDF rasterisation and up to twenty vision calls on the event loop
findings.evidence: routers/banking.py:761-762 `async def upload_statement`, :956 `async def inspect_statement_file`, :994 `async def preview_statement_with_mapping` — the only three async routes in the router (every other route is a plain `def`, which FastAPI runs in a threadpool). Their bodies are fully synchronous: `_read_statement_file` (routers/banking.py:655-741) calls `parse_statement_detailed` → `_pdf_rows` → pdfplumber (domain/banking/normalizer.py:839-874), then `vision.page_images` rasterises up to MAX_PAGES = 20 pages at 150 dpi (domain/banking/vision.py:70-133), then `vision.read_statement` makes one BLOCKING Gemini call per page (vision.py:212-246, services/statement_vision.py:33-42). Nothing is awaited and nothing runs in a thread.
findings.ca_experience: One CA uploading a 20-page scanned statement freezes the entire API process for every other user of the firm — the API runs as a single Render service in Singapore. Other screens hang and then show the generic error card. The uploading CA also has no progress indication for a request that can run for minutes; `uploadStatement` in apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:917-928 uses a bare fetch with no AbortController, so the browser waits until the platform proxy gives up.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and QuickBooks both process a statement upload asynchronously and show an import job with progress; neither holds an HTTP request open across an OCR run.
findings.suggested_fix: Cheapest correct fix: make the three routes plain `def` so Starlette runs them in the threadpool — the file read is the only genuinely async part and can be handled with `file.file.read()`. Then chunk the vision path: rasterise and read pages in batches with the client looping, the way Entries already loops redraft and pass-ready, so a long scan reports progress instead of occupying one request.

findings.title: Two genuinely identical transactions on a statement with no balance column are silently merged into one
findings.evidence: domain/banking/dedup.py:18-40 — `transaction_hash` is over (client, bank account, date, debit, credit, BALANCE, description, reference). services/banking_service.py:171-187 drops within-file duplicates keeping the first, and reports the loss only as `duplicates_skipped`. When the statement carries no balance column — most PDF statements, per the module's own note in domain/banking/tie_out.py:13-15 — every row's balance_paise is 0, so the balance term stops discriminating. I verified in this session: `transaction_hash("c1","a1","2026-04-10",50000,0,0,"UPI/DR/RAMESH KUMAR",None)` computed twice gives the same hash. The tie-out cannot catch it either: statement_check runs on `txns` BEFORE dedup (routers/banking.py:849-853), so the totals agree and the import reports itself verified.
findings.ca_experience: Two ₹500 UPI payments to the same payee on the same day, on a PDF statement with no reference column, become one ₹500 line. The client's bank balance in the books is ₹500 higher than the bank's, the expense is understated by ₹500, and the import screen says "verified — every line was read" with "1 line was already in and was skipped". The CA finds it at reconciliation, if at all.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and QuickBooks dedupe on the bank's own transaction id from the feed, and on manual import they flag a possible duplicate for the user to accept or reject rather than dropping it. Tally's Excel import does not dedupe at all — it imports both and lets the user see them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the row's ordinal position within the file to the hash, so two identical rows are two rows. Then move the WITHIN-FILE duplicate drop from silent to reported: if two rows in one file hash identically, keep both and let the cross-file check (which is what idempotent re-import actually needs) do the deduping. At minimum, run statement_check on the deduped set so a merged row breaks the totals.

findings.title: Auto-match never suggests a part payment against a partially-paid invoice, because the amount band is taken on the document TOTAL
findings.evidence: services/bank_matching_service.py:300-336 — `_fetch_invoice_pool` bands the SQL query on `total_paise`, and `_invoices_from` filters again with `self._in_band(int(r.get("total_paise") or 0), amount)`, setting `Candidate.amount_paise = total` and `outstanding_paise = total - paid` only as an extra scoring signal. Bills do the same on `net_payable_paise` (:338-385). domain/banking/matcher.py:167-182 computes `difference = c.amount_paise - txn_amount` and CONTINUES (skips the candidate) when the bank line is short by more than NEAR_MATCH_BAND_BPS = 2500 (25%, matcher.py:46). So a ₹2,00,000 receipt against a ₹3,00,000 invoice with ₹1,00,000 already paid is 33% short of the total and is dropped, even though it settles the outstanding exactly. domain/banking/candidate_search.py does lift the band, but it ranks by `abs(h.difference_paise)` against the total too (:150-157), so the same document is described as "short by ₹1,00,000 — consistent with … TDS" (candidate_search.py:171-177).
findings.ca_experience: Staged payments are the norm in Indian SME practice. The second and third instalments against an invoice show no suggestion at all on the Entries row — the line reads "From whom, or which ledger?" — so the CA has to open the line, use Find Match, and read a "short by ₹1,00,000, consistent with TDS" label that is nonsense. The settlement itself works correctly (bank_posting_service._settle_doc allocates against true outstanding), so this is purely a suggestion failure, but it is the failure a CA notices on every instalment.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books offers an invoice whose BALANCE DUE matches the deposit and lets you apply a partial payment. Tally's bill-wise details are built entirely around Against Ref / On Account allocation across part payments. QuickBooks matches on open balance, not on invoice total.
findings.suggested_fix: Band and score on OUTSTANDING, not on the document total: use `total_paise - paid_paise` for invoices and the equivalent for bills in both the pool query and `_in_band`, set `Candidate.amount_paise` to the outstanding figure, and keep the total for the label only. `difference_paise` then means what the row says it means, and the TDS shape is detected against the right base.

findings.title: The rule engine is one case-insensitive substring plus an amount range and a direction — no regex, no multiple conditions, no payee/reference field, no split action, no priority
findings.evidence: domain/banking/rules.py:52-69 `rule_matches` is the whole engine: `pattern not in narration.lower()`, an amount min/max, and a txn_type of debit/credit/any. `RuleSuggestion` (:31-49) carries only a category, ONE account_id, a narration, a GST rate and an interstate flag — a rule can never propose a split across ledgers, a party (customer/vendor), or a TDS treatment. Precedence is creation order only (routers/banking.py:2042-2044 and :2065 `.order("created_at")`); there is no priority column and no way to reorder. The UI matches: apps/web/components/banking/RulesTab.tsx:233-245 exposes exactly narration-contains, min, max, direction.
findings.ca_experience: A CA cannot write "NEFT from any of these three customers → Trade Receivables, set the party", or "salary batch → split 60% Salaries / 40% Director's Remuneration", or "EMI to HDFC → principal to Loan, interest to Interest Expense". Every EMI, every payroll batch and every mixed payment stays a manual split, twelve times a year per client. And because the first matching rule wins with no way to reorder, a broad rule written early permanently shadows a narrow one written later.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books bank rules support multiple criteria with AND/OR over description, payee, reference number and amount, with contains / starts with / is operators, and actions that set the category, the payee and the tax. QuickBooks bank rules do the same plus rule priority and split lines by percentage or amount. This is the single biggest gap against both.
findings.suggested_fix: Three increments, in value order: (1) add a `priority` integer and order by it — one column, one migration; (2) let a rule carry several conditions over description/reference/amount with contains/starts-with/equals; (3) let a rule name split legs (percentage or fixed) reusing domain/banking/splits.build_split_lines, which already exists and is tested. Keep the trusted-rule CHECK in step.

findings.title: Deleting a matching rule silently strips the trusted-rule attribution from every entry it posted, and needs only banking.write
findings.evidence: routers/banking.py:2166-2181 `delete_rule` hard-DELETEs the row on `rbac("banking", "write")` (Executive+), with no audit_log write, and its docstring justifies this as "A rule is configuration, not a financial record — it has never written anything to the ledger." That is no longer true: migration 322 added `posted_by_rule_id UUID REFERENCES public.bank_matching_rules(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` on bank_transactions, and services/bank_entry_service.py:536-551 stamps it plus an audit row whenever a trusted rule passes a line. Promotion to trusted is deliberately gated on `banking.approve` (Manager+, routers/banking.py:2118-2129), but deletion is not.
findings.ca_experience: The register sentence the design promises — "Passed by rule Bank charges, trusted by Priya on 3 Sep" (docs/architecture/09-bank-entries.md) — becomes blank on every entry the rule posted, and the Rules tab's "what it has passed" count disappears with it. An Executive can erase a Manager's authorisation trail for hundreds of auto-posted journals with one click, and there is no audit_log row saying the rule ever existed.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books keeps the rule name on the transaction's audit trail after the rule is deleted. QuickBooks records "Added by rule <name>" in the audit log independently of the rule row.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to delete a rule that has posted anything (`posted_by_rule_id` references exist) — deactivate it instead, which the endpoint already supports; require `banking.approve` to delete a rule that is or has been trusted; and write the whole rule row to audit_log in the same transaction, the way the journal deletes do.

findings.title: The exception-rules engine — materiality, duplicates, cash withdrawals, new payees — is complete, tested, and wired to nothing
findings.evidence: domain/banking/exceptions.py is 315 lines implementing `_above_materiality`, `_short_settlement`, `_weak_match`, `_new_payee`, `_unusual_account`, `_cash_withdrawal`, `_duplicate_suspect` with per-client policy thresholds. Its docstring (:20-22) says the context-gathering lives in `services/bank_exception_service.py` — that file DOES NOT EXIST (`ls apps/api/services/bank_exception_service.py` → no such file). A repo-wide grep for `banking.exceptions` / `bank_exception` returns exactly two hits: the module itself and tests/test_bank_exception_rules.py (25 tests). Nothing else imports it. The related column tells the same story: `needs_review` is only ever written FALSE (services/bank_matching_service.py:816, services/bank_posting_service.py:1060) — nothing sets it True — yet services/bank_register_service.py:41,115 exposes a `needs_review` status filter and apps/web/components/banking/BankBook.tsx:80 renders it as a "Needs review" option in the Bank Book dropdown.
findings.ca_experience: There is no partner review list. A partner has no screen that says "these eleven lines are worth looking at this month" — an amount over materiality, a cash withdrawal over ₹50,000, a payee never seen before, a possible duplicate a week apart. And the Bank Book's "Needs review" filter always returns an empty table, which reads as "nothing needs review" rather than "this filter does nothing".
findings.market_standard: This is where the product could beat everyone — Tally, Zoho and QuickBooks all lack a risk-based partner review over the bank feed; it is exactly the kind of analytics the owner wants CAs addicted to. The work is already done and unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the missing `bank_exception_service` (gather the payee/account context the pure module wants), store the flags on the row or compute them per page, and surface them as a fourth Entries filter or a partner dashboard card. Until then, remove the "Needs review" option from the Bank Book so it does not lie, and mark the module's tests as covering an unwired feature.

findings.title: A PDF whose first page has ruled table lines and whose later pages do not silently loses the later pages
findings.evidence: domain/banking/normalizer.py:846-860 `_pdf_rows` loops every page collecting `page.extract_tables()`, then `if rows: return rows` — the geometric fallback `_rows_by_position` runs ONLY when NO page produced a ruled table anywhere in the document. A statement whose first page is ruled and whose continuation pages are not therefore returns page 1 only. Separately, `_rows_by_position` (:908-951) locates a header line per page and `if header is None: return []`, so a continuation page that does not repeat its column headings contributes nothing. Neither case raises; both come back as a short, well-formed row set.
findings.ca_experience: A five-page bank PDF imports as one page. If the statement prints its own Grand Total or the CA typed the balances, the tie-out refuses the import with a confusing message; if it does neither, the import succeeds with `verified: false` and an amber "nothing confirmed that every line was read" note that is easy to click past — and four pages of transactions are simply not in the books.
findings.market_standard: Dedicated PDF-to-Tally converters (the small industry this feature exists to replace) handle mixed-ruling documents by falling back per page. Zoho Books does not accept PDF at all, so the feature itself is ahead of the market — the per-page fallback is what makes it trustworthy.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the strategy per page, not per document: for each page, take `extract_tables()` if it yields rows, otherwise `_rows_by_position(page)`. Carry the header line found on the first page forward to pages that do not repeat it. Both are small changes inside `_pdf_rows`.

findings.title: Transfer detection scans only the newest 1,000 lines, and is re-run from scratch for every 100-line redraft chunk
findings.evidence: services/bank_transfer_service.py:29 `SCAN_LIMIT = 1000` and :55-58 `.order("transaction_date", desc=True).limit(SCAN_LIMIT)` — a hard cap, not `fetch_all`, and the only bank read that is not covered by tests/test_bank_reads_are_complete.py. services/bank_entry_service.py:417-431 `_pairs_by_txn` calls `detect_pairs` for the WHOLE client, and it is invoked once per redraft chunk (bank_entry_service.py:372, inside `redraft`, which processes REDRAFT_CHUNK = 100 lines). domain/banking/transfers.py:158-171 then builds every out×in candidate pairing, which is quadratic in the scanned set.
findings.ca_experience: Two effects. (1) On a client with more than about a year of statement lines, an inter-account transfer in an older month is never proposed — the CA codes both halves separately and the P&L is overstated by the transfer, which is precisely what the feature exists to prevent. (2) Proposing for a 3,000-line back-log import runs the 1,000-row fetch and the quadratic pair scan thirty times, adding thirty Mumbai round trips and a lot of CPU to an operation the CA is watching a progress bar for.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and QuickBooks both detect transfers across the whole account history, and neither recomputes the candidate set per page of the review queue.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the pair index ONCE per redraft run and pass it into each chunk (it is already a parameterised argument — `detect_pairs(..., txns=...)`). Replace the flat 1,000-row cap with a date window anchored on the chunk's own lines (± DEFAULT_WINDOW_DAYS), which is both complete and far smaller.

findings.title: The nightly trusted-rule sweep will auto-post a line the CA coded themselves, and credit it to the person who trusted the rule
findings.evidence: services/bank_entry_service.py:635-651 `pass_ready(only_trusted=True)` selects rows on `entry_state = 'ready'` AND `draft_rule_id IN (trusted rules)` — it does not exclude a row that is ready because a HUMAN coded it. For such a row `pass_entry` (:497) skips `_apply_draft` (correctly, `E.coded_by_a_human` is true) and posts the CA's own coding, but with `actor = rule.get("trusted_by")` (:648) and then stamps `posted_by_rule_id` and an audit row with `source: bank_trusted_rule` (:536-551). Nothing clears `draft_rule_id` when a CA sets an account: banking_service.set_account (banking_service.py:307-333) writes account_id/category only, and migration 322's trigger clears `draft_error` but not the draft. jobs/bank_trusted_rules_job.py:75-83 runs this unattended every day.
findings.ca_experience: The CA opens a bank-charge line that a trusted rule proposed, decides it is actually a Loan Processing Fee, picks that ledger, and moves on without pressing Pass. Overnight the sweep posts it — a journal the CA never authorised, with `created_by` set to the Manager who trusted an unrelated rule and an audit trail saying the rule did it. The amount is right; the authorisation and the attribution are not.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books auto-categorisation rules apply only to uncategorised feed transactions and never act on a transaction a user has touched. QuickBooks rules likewise stop at the first manual edit.
findings.suggested_fix: In `pass_ready`, when `only_trusted` is set, skip any row where `E.coded_by_a_human(row)` is true — the rule's authority covers the rule's proposal, not a human's different answer. Cheap and exactly matches the design's own reasoning in docs/architecture/09-bank-entries.md.

findings.title: Undo reverses the journal of a line that sits inside a completed, certified reconciliation, with no check and no warning
findings.evidence: services/bank_posting_service.py:690-820 `undo` checks match_status, the journal's source_type and the period lock — I grepped services/bank_posting_service.py, services/bank_matching_service.py and services/bank_entry_service.py for `reconciliation_id` and there are ZERO hits. So a line with `reconciliation_id` pointing at a session whose status is 'completed' is reversed like any other. The certified report itself is safe (bank_reconciliation_service.py:407-413 freezes a snapshot at completion), and the divergence surfaces later as `opening_balance_check` (domain/banking/reconciliation.py:78-111) the next time someone opens a session on that account — a warning, deliberately not a block.
findings.ca_experience: A CA undoes a March line in June. March's BRS PDF still says it tied out; the books no longer agree with it. The register shows the line as 'R' (reconciled) with no journal — domain/banking/register.py:126-144 derives the flag from `reconciliation_id` alone. Nobody is told at the moment of the undo; the only signal is a mismatch figure on the NEXT reconciliation, which reads like a different problem.
findings.market_standard: QuickBooks warns explicitly ("this transaction is reconciled — changing it will affect your reconciliation") and marks the period. Tally refuses to alter the bank date of a reconciled voucher without re-opening the reconciliation. Zoho Books requires you to un-reconcile first.
findings.suggested_fix: In `undo` (and in `unmatch`), read the line's `reconciliation_id` and its session status. If the session is completed, either refuse with "this line is part of a completed reconciliation for <period> — reopen it first" (the reopen path with its mandatory reason already exists), or require an explicit acknowledgement and clear `reconciliation_id` so the register stops claiming 'R'.

findings.title: The import module's most important refusals reach the CA as raw JSON: "API error 422: {\"detail\":\"...\"}"
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/api/index.ts:917-928 `uploadStatement` throws `new Error(\`API error ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}\`)`. The very next function, `postStatementForm` (:930-944), does the right thing with `errorMessage(res)` (:450-476), which unwraps `detail` — and the comment there even says "A 422 here is a real answer … and its message is written for the CA". AccountsPanel.tsx:704-707 renders whatever the error's `message` is. The sentences being mangled are the carefully-written ones in domain/banking/tie_out.py:110-115 and :264-268 ("The statement does not add up. Opening ₹1,30,000.00 plus credits …") and the scan refusals in routers/banking.py:706-741.
findings.ca_experience: The one moment the module most needs to be understood — an import refused because the arithmetic does not land — the CA is shown a developer string wrapped around the explanation. The Indian-grouped rupee formatting in tie_out._r, written specifically so the figures can be compared against the paper statement, is buried inside escaped JSON.
findings.market_standard: Every competitor shows a plain-language import error. This is not a market gap, it is a one-line regression against the codebase's own standard two functions below.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `errorMessage(res)` in `uploadStatement`, exactly as `postStatementForm` does. One line. Keep `looksLikeAFormatProblem` working by matching on the unwrapped sentence.

findings.title: Two banking screens parse typed rupees outside lib/money/rupeeInput, against the "one parser, and only one" rule
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md, "Money in the browser — one parser, and only one": all 61 call sites converted, with three named exceptions, all in gstLine. Two banking call sites are not among them. (1) apps/web/lib/banking/splitLegs.ts:36-42 `rupeesToPaise` does `Number(cleaned)` then `Math.round(n * 100)`, and apps/web/components/banking/SplitAcrossLedgersModal.tsx:140 sends its output straight to the server as `amount_paise`. It strips commas, so the 1,25,000 disaster does not apply, but it accepts "1e3" as ₹1,000 and silently rounds a three-decimal entry rather than refusing. (2) apps/web/components/banking/RulesTab.tsx:104 `boundToPaise = rsToP(parseFloat(v) || 0)`, where shared.ts:29 `rsToP` is `Math.round(rs * 100)` — literally the form CLAUDE.md says was eradicated. Its inputs are `type="number"` (RulesTab.tsx:235,240), which blunts it: a browser reports value="" for "1,25,000", so the bound silently vanishes rather than becoming ₹1. Every other banking screen uses the right parser (ReconcileTab.tsx:11,100; AccountsPanel.tsx:17,353,597-598).
findings.ca_experience: A CA typing an amount band of 1,25,000 into a rule sees the digits in the box, presses Save, and the rule is stored with no upper bound at all — it then fires on lines it should not, and if the rule is trusted it posts them. In the split modal, a leg typed as 12.345 becomes ₹12.35 with no warning.
findings.market_standard: Not a market issue — an internal consistency issue with a documented failure history in this repo.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace both with `paiseFromRupeeInput` and handle its null as a refusal, the way ReconcileTab already does with its NOT_AN_AMOUNT message. Delete `rsToP` from components/banking/shared.ts so it cannot come back.

findings.title: There is no cash book — no cash vouchers, no cash register, no petty-cash screen
findings.evidence: A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for 'cash book', 'cashbook', 'petty cash' and 'petty_cash' across apps/api and apps/web returns four hits and none of them is a feature: services/coa_seed_service.py:52 seeds a "1002 Petty Cash" ledger, tests/test_bank_account_first_coding.py uses it as a fixture, domain/dpdp/retention.py:111 mentions the statutory cash book in prose, and apps/web/components/banking/EntryDetailModal.tsx:514 uses the phrase in help text. apps/web/app/clients/[id]/reports/ contains ageing, bank-book, ratios and trend — no cash book. The only route into cash is `account_category` deriving Transfer when a CA picks a Cash-subtype ledger on a bank line (domain/banking/account_category.py).
findings.ca_experience: Every SME client of an Indian CA runs cash. Wages, conveyance, tea, freight, small purchases — hundreds of vouchers a month that never touch a bank statement. There is no way to enter them as cash vouchers, no running cash balance, no negative-cash check, and no Cash Book report to print. The CA has to keep that half of the client's books in Tally, which defeats the whole premise of the platform.
findings.market_standard: The Cash Book is one of Tally's headline reports and cash Receipt/Payment/Contra vouchers are its most-used entry screens; Busy and Marg are the same. Zoho Books has Cash accounts with the same register as bank accounts. Every one of them has a negative-cash warning.
findings.suggested_fix: The kernel already supports it — Receipt/Payment/Contra, the posting map, the register and the running-balance code are all account-agnostic. Add a Cash account type alongside bank_accounts (or reuse it with a Cash subtype), a voucher entry screen, and reuse domain/banking/register.py for the Cash Book report. Add a negative-balance warning, which is the one cash-specific rule.

findings.title: Credit-card accounts are not supported at all
findings.evidence: migrations/054_v13_payroll_assets_banking.sql:100-101 — `account_type CHECK (account_type IN ('Current','Savings','Cash Credit','Overdraft'))`. There is no 'Credit Card'. apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:416 offers exactly those four. The ledger creation path (routers/banking.py:250) would in any case give a card an Asset ledger, and the posting map treats every statement line as money in or out of a bank asset (domain/banking/posting_map.py:43-78).
findings.ca_experience: A company credit card is normal for any SME with travel or online spend. The CA cannot set the card up as an account, so the card statement cannot be imported, its expenses cannot be coded through the bank workflow, and the monthly card payment from the bank posts to whatever ledger someone picks — with the underlying expenses never recorded from the card statement at all.
findings.market_standard: QuickBooks and Zoho Books both have first-class credit-card accounts (a liability, with the payment recorded as a transfer from bank to card). Tally handles it as a liability ledger with a card statement imported like any other.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Credit Card' to the account_type CHECK and the picker, give it a Liability ledger (same change as BANK-02), and make the card-payment line a Contra between the bank and the card ledger — the transfer machinery already handles that shape.

findings.title: A statement imported without a bank account posts every line to a generic "Bank" ledger and is invisible to the register, the reconciliation and the account filter
findings.evidence: bank_transactions has no bank_account_id column (migrations/006_transactions_bank_compliance.sql:90-109 and nothing since adds one); every account-scoped read resolves it through the statement (services/bank_entry_service.py:92-99 `_statement_ids`, services/bank_transfer_service.py:41-46 `_account_by_statement`, services/bank_register_service.py:76-84, services/bank_reconciliation_service.py:55-58). `bank_account_id` is Optional on both import entry points: models/banking.py:83 (`StatementImportIn`) and routers/banking.py:768. When it is absent, services/bank_posting_service.py:68-105 `_resolve_bank` falls through to `phase2_journal_service._find_account(db, firm_id, client_id, "%Bank%", system_key="bank")` — the firm's generic master Bank account.
findings.ca_experience: Lines imported this way appear in the Entries queue (client-scoped) and can be passed, but every journal debits or credits a generic Bank ledger rather than the client's actual bank account. They never appear in any Bank Book, never appear in any reconciliation, and the account filter cannot find them. The web UI does always send an account (AccountsPanel.tsx:684 refuses without one), so this is reachable through the API and through the JSON /statements/import endpoint rather than through the normal screen.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and QuickBooks make the account mandatory on a statement import — there is no unassigned state.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `bank_account_id` required on both import endpoints (it is already validated for ownership at banking_service.py:164-169 when supplied), and make `_resolve_bank`'s generic fallback raise rather than post to a master Bank account — an unattributable bank line should refuse, not guess. Longer term, denormalise bank_account_id onto bank_transactions so every scoped read is one filter instead of a statement-id round trip.

findings.title: The reconciliation shows only POSTED statement lines, so an unposted line in the period produces a difference with nothing on screen naming it
findings.evidence: services/bank_reconciliation_service.py:60-72 `_posted_account_txns` ends with `return [t for t in rows if t.get("posted_journal_id")]`. `_classify` (:84-100) therefore buckets only posted lines into reconciled / unreconciled / exceptions, and `_compute_report` (:602-628) renders only those three lists. `complete()` (:389-395) refuses on unreconciled POSTED lines with a count — it says nothing about lines that were never posted. The screen (apps/web/components/banking/ReconcileTab.tsx:565) offers exactly those three views.
findings.ca_experience: A CA opens a reconciliation for April, ticks everything the screen offers, and the tie-out still shows a ₹1,84,300 difference. Nothing on the Reconcile tab lists the forty April lines that are still sitting unpassed in Entries, and the completion refusal does not mention them either. The CA's next move is either to hunt through another tab or to type the difference into Adjustments (see BANK-05).
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books shows uncategorised statement lines inside the reconciliation with a "categorise" action. QuickBooks blocks reconciliation and names the count of unreviewed transactions in the period.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fourth bucket — in-period statement lines with no journal — computed from the same fetch (drop the `posted_journal_id` filter and split), show it as a "Not yet passed (N)" view with a link into Entries filtered to that account and period, and name it in the completion refusal.

findings.title: Bank-charge input tax credit is posted with no supplier GSTIN or invoice reference, so it can never be reconciled to GSTR-2B
findings.evidence: domain/banking/charge_gst.py:74-110 splits the inclusive charge and services/bank_posting_service.py:233-274 `_charge_lines` books the tax to the GST Input Credit account (CGST Act s.16, cited at charge_gst.py:19-21). The journal it produces carries only `account_id`, `debit_paise`, `credit_paise` (domain/banking/charge_gst.build_inclusive_lines) — no counterparty GSTIN, no supplier invoice number, no place-of-supply record beyond the boolean. The rule that supplies the rate (`bank_matching_rules`, migration 254) carries `suggested_gst_rate_bps` and `suggested_is_interstate` and nothing identifying the bank as a supplier.
findings.ca_experience: The ITC on bank charges lands in the GST Input ledger and reduces the net payable, but when the CA runs the 2A/2B reconciliation it appears as credit claimed with no counterparty invoice to match — an unexplained difference every month. Under s.16(2)(aa) credit is only available if the supplier's invoice appears in GSTR-2B, so this is credit the CA has to defend without the evidence the product could have captured.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books requires a vendor on a GST-bearing expense so it flows into the purchase register and the 2B match. Tally requires a party ledger with a GSTIN on any voucher claiming input credit — you cannot claim ITC on a bank charge without one.
findings.suggested_fix: Let a bank account (or the rule) carry the bank's GSTIN and state, stamp it onto the charge journal and onto a purchase-register row, so bank-charge ITC joins the same 2A/2B reconciliation as every other input credit. At minimum, tag these journals so the GST reconciliation can report them as a named category rather than an unexplained difference.

findings.title: Every imported statement shows an amber "pending" chip forever — import_status is written once and never advanced
findings.evidence: services/banking_service.py:204 writes `"import_status": "pending"` on the bank_statements row. A repo-wide grep for `import_status` across apps/api returns exactly two hits: that line, and the CHECK constraint in migrations/006_transactions_bank_compliance.sql:81. Nothing ever updates it. apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:132-136 maps pending→amber, reviewed→blue, posted→green, and :243 renders the chip in the Status column of the statements table.
findings.ca_experience: The Accounts panel is the screen a CA opens to check what has been brought in. Every statement they have ever imported and fully passed still shows an amber "pending" badge. The one status column on that table conveys nothing, and looks like a backlog.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books shows a per-statement progress ("312 of 312 categorised"). QuickBooks shows the count still in For Review per import.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drive it from the lines (pending → reviewed once every line has left needs_you, posted once every line is passed or set aside — a cheap SQL count on the existing entry_state index), or drop the column from the table and show "N of M passed" instead, which is what the CA actually wants to know.

findings.title: Six statement layouts are auto-detected; every other bank needs a manual mapping, and the mapping cannot be shared between accounts or clients
findings.evidence: domain/banking/normalizer.py:97-125 `_ADAPTERS` holds exactly six: hdfc, generic_cheque, sbi, icici, axis, generic, generic_amount_drcr (six adapter keys plus the amount/drcr variant). `detect_format` (:128-174) picks between them on header words; anything else raises the "Unsupported bank statement format" message at :216-243. The escape hatch is a per-account column mapping keyed on a header fingerprint: services/bank_column_mapping_service.py, saved against `(firm_id, bank_account_id, header_fingerprint)` and looked up the same way (routers/banking.py:840-844, 892-903). There is no firm-level or bank-name-level reuse.
findings.ca_experience: The design decision not to guess eight more adapters is right and CLAUDE.md-consistent. But a firm with thirty clients banking at Kotak maps the Kotak layout thirty times — once per bank account — even though the header fingerprint is identical. And there is no library screen showing which layouts the firm has taught; only a per-account list (GET /statements/column-mappings).
findings.market_standard: Perfios, Setu and the PDF-to-Tally converters ship hundreds of bank templates. Zoho Books remembers a CSV mapping per organisation and offers it for any account. Tally has no mapping at all — you must reshape the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back from the account-scoped mapping to a firm-scoped one on the same header fingerprint before asking again — the fingerprint already makes reuse safe, which is the whole argument in normalizer.py:591-607. Add a Settings screen listing the firm's learned layouts with the bank name, so a CA can see and correct them. Adding real adapters, if ever, should come from real files the firm has already mapped.

findings.title: An opening balance can be saved with no opening-balance date, and the Bank Book then folds pre-opening lines into the running balance
findings.evidence: models/banking.py:20-21 — `opening_balance_paise: int = 0` and `opening_balance_date: Optional[str] = None`, no cross-validation. apps/web/components/banking/AccountsPanel.tsx:419-427 renders both fields with neither required and no check that a non-zero balance has a date. domain/banking/register.py:176-179 then computes `precedes = bool(opening_date and d and d < opening_date)` — with a null date NOTHING precedes, so every imported line is added on top of the opening figure, and `delta = stated_int - running` (:184) compares the result against the bank's own balance column.
findings.ca_experience: A CA enters ₹4,50,000 as the opening balance, leaves the date blank, then imports the full year including months before that figure. The Bank Book's running balance is overstated by every pre-opening movement, and the self-check reports a divergence on the very first line — which reads as a parsing or import fault rather than a setup mistake. The register's careful note-2 protection is silently disabled.
findings.market_standard: Tally requires an opening balance to be entered against the books-beginning date; there is no undated opening balance. Zoho Books requires an "as of" date on a bank opening balance.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `opening_balance_date` whenever `opening_balance_paise` is non-zero, in `BankAccountIn`/`BankAccountUpdateIn` and in the form. Default it to the client's books-beginning date. Where existing rows have a balance and no date, surface it as a named setup gap on the account row rather than silently mis-computing.

findings.title: The narration parser extracts channel, UTR, VPA, IFSC and counterparty but never a cheque number
findings.evidence: domain/banking/narration.py:104-119 `ParsedNarration` has raw, channel, utr, vpa, counterparty, ifsc, direction, tokens — no cheque number field. `_CHANNELS` (:51) recognises CHQ/CHEQUE/CLG/MICR as a channel, but `_is_noise_word` (:155-167) discards any pure-digit token, so the number itself is thrown away. The number IS captured when the export has its own cheque column (the `ref` index in the hdfc/generic_cheque/sbi/axis adapters, normalizer.py:99-113 → `reference_no`), and it is shown by the register (domain/banking/register.py:91) and the reconciliation report (bank_reconciliation_service.py:609).
findings.ca_experience: For a PDF or scanned statement where the cheque number appears inside the narration rather than in its own column, the CA loses it. That matters most for exactly the report that needs it — the BRS, where an unpresented cheque is identified by its instrument number.
findings.market_standard: Tally's BRS lists the instrument number against every reconciling item, and its bank-statement import maps a cheque-number column explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `cheque_no` field to ParsedNarration, populated when the channel is CHEQUE/CLG and a 6-digit token is present, and fall back to it when `reference_no` is empty. Small, and it becomes load-bearing the moment BANK-04 is built.

findings.title: A statement's opening/closing-balance row becomes a zero-amount bank line that clogs the queue and can never be passed
findings.evidence: domain/banking/normalizer.py:400-459 `_rows_to_txns` skips a row only when it has fewer than three non-empty cells, or no parseable date, or no description. A row like `01/04/2026 | OPENING BALANCE | | | | 1000.00` has a date, a description and a balance, so it is emitted with debit_paise = 0 and credit_paise = 0. I verified this: the three-transaction CSV I parsed in this session included the "OPENING BAL" row as a transaction. Note the amount/drcr branch DOES guard this (`if amount == 0 … continue`, :444) — the two-column branch does not. Downstream, `_plan` refuses it with "Transaction has zero amount" (services/bank_posting_service.py:290-291), so it can never be passed.
findings.ca_experience: Every imported statement leaves one or two permanent "needs you" lines — Opening Balance, Closing Balance, B/F — that the CA cannot pass and must Set aside one by one. On a firm importing 50 statements a month that is 50-100 pointless clicks, and the "33 need you" counter on Entries is never truthful.
findings.market_standard: Zoho Books and QuickBooks both drop zero-amount rows on import. Tally's Excel import ignores rows with no debit and no credit.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip a row with no debit and no credit in the two-column branch of `_rows_to_txns`, matching what the amount/drcr branch already does. Zero-amount rows carry no money and no information the balance column does not already give.

maturity.rationale: The engine is genuinely strong and in places ahead of anything on the Indian market: three independent import verifications that refuse before writing, a PDF text parser with geometric column recovery (TallyPrime cannot import a PDF at all), a vision path whose totals are read by a deliberately independent second call, a single posting path that refuses to debit and credit the same ledger, an exact tax-inclusive GST split, a transfer double-count guard, an append-only undo that revokes party credit and re-uses an existing reversal, and an entry_state column maintained by a trigger with a Python twin pinned by a real parity test. The screens are honest — a verified import and an unverified one cannot look the same. What holds it back from an A is that the pillar a CA judges the module by is the wrong shape: the document titled "Bank Reconciliation Statement" is a statement-line tick-off with no unpresented cheques and no deposits in transit, and it carries an unexplained Adjustments plug that can force it to tie out and be certified. Alongside that sit two ledger-classification faults that put wrong figures on the balance sheet (OD/CC accounts booked as assets, foreign-currency accounts posted at 1:1), no cash book at all, no credit cards, no way to undo a mis-imported statement, an import that can be falsely refused by a page subtotal, and a rule engine markedly thinner than Zoho's or QuickBooks'. None of those is deep — the kernel underneath is right and most are days of work, not months.
maturity.would_a_ca_buy_this_module_alone: Not yet — the import and coding loop is better than anything in the Indian market, but a CA will open Reconcile first, find it is not the BRS they have prepared every month of their career, and no cash book anywhere, and conclude they still need Tally beside it.

open_questions_for_owner: The BRS is the module's shop window and it is currently the wrong document. Do you want the classic two-sided Indian BRS — Balance as per Cash Book, add cheques issued not presented, less cheques deposited not credited, Balance as per Pass Book — built on the book side (weeks), or is the statement tick-off deliberate and the PDF simply mistitled?

Is the cash book in scope? Every SME client runs cash, the kernel already supports Receipt/Payment/Contra on any ledger, and its absence is the clearest single reason a CA keeps Tally open beside this. Or is cash deliberately out of scope for now?

Overdraft and Cash Credit accounts are offered in the account-type dropdown but always given an Asset ledger, and the ledger picker will not show a Liability. Fixing it changes existing clients' balance sheets — do you want a migration that re-classifies existing OD/CC ledgers and reports what moved, or a forward-only fix with the old ones flagged?

Multi-currency bank accounts are permitted today and post at 1:1. Do you want them refused until an FX path exists (one line, honest, today) or the FX path built (days)? Is any live client actually using a non-INR bank account?

The reconciliation's Adjustments field is a free plug with no reason and no journal. Should a non-zero adjustment (a) require a substantive reason like the reopen path already does, (b) require Manager approval, or (c) become an actual posted journal so the books and the certificate agree?

domain/banking/exceptions.py is a complete, 25-test, partner-review engine — materiality, duplicates, cash withdrawals, new payees — wired to nothing, and its service file was never written. It is the closest thing in this module to the analytics you want CAs addicted to. Was it deliberately parked, and do you want it finished?

How far do you want the rule engine pushed against Zoho and QuickBooks? A priority column alone would fix the "first rule wins forever" problem in hours; multi-condition rules and split actions are weeks. Which do your first CAs actually ask for?

Trusted rules currently post unattended overnight, including over lines the CA has hand-coded differently. Should a line a human has touched be permanently exempt from the sweep, or is posting the human's own coding acceptable?

Should a mis-imported statement be deletable? It requires hard-deleting bank_transactions, which sits close to the immutability rules — is "unposted and unreconciled lines only, with the whole statement written to audit_log" the boundary you want?

The Bank Book fetches the whole account and computes the running balance in Python, which the reporting rule forbids. Is a SQL function plus a parity test (the cash_flow_report pattern) the right investment now, or is it acceptable until a client's line count actually hurts?
strengths: The import verification is three independent checks that refuse BEFORE anything is written, and it is better than anything on the Indian market. `normalizer.balance_agreement` (normalizer.py:609-678) tests consecutive deltas against the bank's own running balance and detects a newest-first statement rather than calling it an error; `tie_out.totals_agreement` (tie_out.py:224-269) sums against the bank's own printed "Grand Total"; `tie_out.tie_out` (:62-116) checks opening + credits − debits = closing. `statement_check` (:272-333) combines them so that either failing refuses the import (routers/banking.py:849-853), and a `verified` flag means an unchecked import and a checked one cannot look the same on screen (AccountsPanel.tsx:747-760).

PDF import with a geometric fallback. `_pdf_rows` (normalizer.py:791-874) tries ruled-table extraction first, then assigns each word to a column by its x-midpoint against the header's own coordinates (`_rows_by_position`, :908-951, with `_merge_label_words` splitting at one em, :883-905). The docstring records exactly why a whitespace split is worse than useless. TallyPrime's own documentation tells users to convert a PDF to CSV first; this reads it.

The vision path's independence argument is the right one and is actually implemented. `read_printed_totals` (vision.py:275-343) is a SECOND model call given the last page alone and shown no transactions, so the totals cannot be a sum of the reading being checked, and it refuses unless the label matches the same `_TOTAL_LABEL` regex the deterministic parser uses and both figures look like money. The gate is applied one page-sized call in, before twenty pages are rasterised (routers/banking.py:721-733).

entry_state is a trigger-maintained column with a Python twin and a real parity test — not a claimed one. Migration 322's `bank_transaction_entry_state()` and `domain/banking/entry.py::entry_state` (:126-147) have the same branches in the same order, and tests/test_bank_entry_state_parity_pg.py parametrises BOTH over the same shared `STATE_TABLE` imported from tests/test_bank_entry.py:42-69, asserting the trigger and the twin agree on every case plus UPDATE-time behaviour Postgres alone can prove.

One posting path, and it refuses the failure mode that balances. `posting_map.build_lines` (:50-67) raises when the bank and counter accounts are the same — an entry that satisfies the double-entry assertion, nets to zero, posts, becomes immutable, and classifies nothing. The comment explaining why nothing else catches it is exactly the standard of reasoning this codebase should be judged by.

The tax-inclusive bank-charge split is exact by construction and direction-aware. `split_inclusive_charge` (charge_gst.py:75-110) backs the taxable value out with integer arithmetic and takes the tax as the REMAINDER so the journal balances with no plug, and `_charge_lines` (bank_posting_service.py:233-274) picks GST Input for money out (s.16) and GST Output for money in (s.9) rather than using one set for both. Place of supply under IGST s.12(12) is stated by the CA on the rule, never inferred from an IFSC.

Undo is a genuine append-only reversal with the hard cases handled. `bank_posting_service.undo` (:690-820) reverses on the original date while the period is open and today's when locked, RE-USES an existing reversal so a retried undo cannot swing the ledger twice, revokes the party credit granted from an overpayment before unsettling the document that produced it, refuses a multi-invoice settlement that belongs to a receipt, and returns the line to `matched` rather than `unmatched` so the CA does not have to re-find the invoice.

Transfer double-counting is prevented structurally, not by convention. `domain/banking/transfers.detect` (:150-224) counts every possible pairing BEFORE the greedy choice so ambiguity can be reported rather than resolved, pairing is written through an RPC (migration 258) so a half-paired state cannot exist, and `_plan` (bank_posting_service.py:346-352) refuses to post the receiving side of an already-posted pair.

The narration parser classifies by SHAPE rather than enumerating bank layouts (narration.py:24-31), and `party_matches` (:265-301) normalises entity suffixes so "Acme Pvt Ltd" matches "ACME PRIVATE LIMITED" — with the single-shared-word coincidence explicitly excluded. Tested by 35 cases in tests/test_bank_narration.py.

Row-addressed authorisation is done properly. `_assert_row_scope` (routers/banking.py:105-133) resolves the row inside the firm and then applies `assert_client_access`, returning 404 for both "no such row" and "not your client"; `_assert_txn_batch_scope` (:143-166) checks every distinct client in a batch BEFORE any row is touched, with the reasoning about ids leaking written down. Every row-addressed banking endpoint uses one of them.

The register self-checks against the bank's own balance column and reports only the FIRST divergence (register.first_divergence, :210-231), because every line below inherits the same offset — and it excludes rows dated before the account's opening-balance date from the arithmetic rather than double-counting them (:176-185). That check is structurally impossible in QuickBooks, which has no bank-stated balance per line.

Reconciliation completion freezes a snapshot (bank_reconciliation_service.py:407-413) so a certified period cannot silently change, reopening requires a substantive reason enforced by both a Pydantic validator and a DB CHECK (models/banking.py:312-329, migration 253), and `opening_suggestion` (:140-215) derives the next period's opening from the previous frozen snapshot and warns when the books have moved under it.

A refused bank-account deletion names the statute, whose duty it is and the date it lapses. services/bank_erasure.py:60-98 splits the retention reason (Companies Act s. 128(5), dated from the newest statement's own period through domain/dpdp/retention.decision_for_record_date) from the referential reason, and refuses to invoke a statute it cannot date.

The frontend genuinely holds no business logic in the core loop: entry_state, the kind, the draft and the register balance are all server-computed and the components say so (BankBook.tsx:24-26, EntriesTab.tsx:74-75). Money is parsed by lib/money/rupeeInput in ReconcileTab and AccountsPanel, and the long jobs are chunked, resumable loops with progress rather than a job table.
subsystem: Banking — statement import (CSV/XLSX/PDF/vision), normalisation, bank entries and drafts, rules and trusted rules, matching, transfers, splits, charges with GST, reconciliation and BRS, bank register/bank book, bank erasure
test_coverage_notes:
Roughly 700 mock-mode tests across ~45 files under apps/api/tests (test_bank_*, test_statement_*, test_reconciliation_*, test_e2e_banking*). I ran tests/test_bank_feed_import.py, test_statement_printed_totals.py, test_bank_entry.py and test_bank_transfers.py together: 120 passed in 5.8s. Depth is real, not decorative — 53 cases on candidate search, 49 on charge-GST posting, 35 on narration parsing, 30 on the vision path with an injected fake model so the real prompt and real refusals are exercised with no key and no traffic.

What is genuinely well pinned. tests/test_bank_entry_state_parity_pg.py is a REAL parity proof, not a claimed one: it imports STATE_TABLE from tests/test_bank_entry.py:42-69 and parametrises both the Postgres trigger and the Python twin over the same 18 cases, plus UPDATE-time draft_error clearing that only a database can show, and tests/test_bank_entry.py:77 asserts every state the trigger can produce appears in the table. tests/test_bank_reads_are_complete.py builds a stub that truncates exactly like PostgREST and proves the register, the categorisation queue and the reconciliation each read past 1,000 rows.

Gaps I can name from the code I read. (1) No test covers a statement that prints a page subtotal labelled "Total" before its Grand Total — I grepped test_statement_printed_totals.py for a subtotal or per-page case and found none, and the behaviour I reproduced is a false refusal of a correct file (BANK-01). (2) No parity test between apps/web/lib/banking/splitLegs.ts and apps/api/domain/banking/splits.py; the repo has only shared/gst-parity-vectors.json, so the browser's split arithmetic and the server's are two implementations with nothing holding them together — exactly the situation CLAUDE.md's cash-flow rule exists to prevent. (3) tests/test_bank_exception_rules.py has 25 passing tests over domain/banking/exceptions.py, which nothing in the product imports — 25 tests of confidence in a feature no CA can reach. (4) domain/banking/transfers is tested only with small in-memory sets, so bank_transfer_service's hard SCAN_LIMIT = 1000 and its per-chunk re-run are not covered by the reads-are-complete suite. (5) No test asserts that a non-INR bank account's statement is handled at all, which is why BANK-03 passes CI. (6) The real-Postgres tests (test_bank_entry_state_parity_pg.py, test_bank_undo_status_vocabulary_pg.py, test_statement_opening_parity_pg.py, test_r253_reconciliation_reopen_pg.py) self-skip without HARNESS_PG, so the parity guarantees hold only in the migration-apply CI job, not in the default run.

I found no test asserting a WRONG statutory behaviour. The GST-on-charges tests (test_bank_charge_gst.py, test_bank_gst_both_directions.py) assert the inclusive split and the input/output direction correctly against s.16 and s.9; the matcher's TDS-shape tests label a shortfall without computing a liability, which is the right line.
what_exists:
Statement import. `POST /api/banking/statements/upload` (routers/banking.py:761) takes a CSV, XLSX, PDF or image. `domain/banking/normalizer.py` detects six layouts from the header row — hdfc, sbi, icici, axis, a six-column cheque layout (generic_cheque, built against a real 33-page Cosmos Co-op statement), a generic Date/Desc/Debit/Credit/Balance, and a generic single-Amount + Dr/Cr variant — validates that the chosen adapter actually fits, and otherwise raises "Unsupported bank statement format". The way past that is an explicit per-account column mapping keyed on a SHA of the header row (`validate_mapping`, `header_fingerprint`, services/bank_column_mapping_service.py), reachable through /statements/inspect and /statements/preview. PDFs are parsed from a text layer, first by ruled-table extraction and then by a geometric fallback that assigns words to columns by x-midpoint. A scanned PDF or phone photo goes to Gemini (`domain/banking/vision.py`, services/statement_vision.py) only when the CA opts in.

Verification. Three checks, in `domain/banking/tie_out.py` and `normalizer.balance_agreement`: the rows against the bank's running-balance column, the rows against the "Grand Total" the bank printed on the file, and opening + credits − debits = closing from two figures the CA types. `statement_check` runs whichever are available; either failing refuses the import before anything is written, and a scan is never imported unverified.

Storage and dedup. `services/banking_service._import_core` fingerprints every row (client, bank account, date, amounts, balance, description, reference), drops within-file and already-stored duplicates, and chunk-inserts into `bank_transactions` under a `(client_id, import_hash)` unique index, with a `bank_statements` header row carrying the period, totals and file metadata.

Entries. Migration 322 put the machine's proposal ON the row (`draft_*` columns) and the state in a trigger-maintained `entry_state` (needs_you / proposed / ready / covered / passed / set_aside) with a Python twin in `domain/banking/entry.py`. `bank_entry_service.redraft` writes each open line's best proposal from four sources — a rule the CA wrote, an open document the matcher ranked, a transfer counterpart, the payee's coding history — graded ready or proposed with a reason sentence. `pass_ready` passes every ready line in chunks of fifty through `bank_posting_service.post`, the one posting path. Endpoints: /entries, /entries/counts, /entries/{id}, /entries/redraft, /entries/pass-ready, /transactions/{id}/pass, plus the older per-line verbs (categorize, match, unmatch, undo, match-multi, ignore, unignore, splits, payee, transfer-pair, attachments, posting-preview, post).

Rules. `bank_matching_rules` with one narration substring, an amount range and a direction, proposing a category, one ledger, a narration and a GST rate/interstate flag. A Manager+ can mark a rule TRUSTED, after which its ready drafts post with no click — on import from the screen, and nightly from jobs/bank_trusted_rules_job.py, with `journal_entries.created_by = trusted_by`.

Posting. `bank_posting_service` resolves the bank ledger from the statement's account, the counter from the category or the CA's pick, builds two-leg, n-leg (splits), contra (transfers) or GST-inclusive charge lines, posts through `phase2_journal_service._create_journal`, then settles the matched invoice or bill against true outstanding with the excess granted as party credit. `undo` reverses append-only.

Reconciliation. Sessions per bank account per period (`bank_reconciliations`), manual tick-off of POSTED statement lines, an arithmetic tie-out with a free Adjustments figure, completion frozen into a snapshot, reopen with a mandatory reason, and a report as JSON, CSV and a "Bank Reconciliation Statement" PDF.

Screens. apps/web/app/clients/[id]/bank is a shell over three tabs — Entries, Reconcile (BRS), Rules — with an Accounts panel and import modal reached from the toolbar, and the Bank Book (register) under Reports.
